audit_findings.title: Required working capital may be absent from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $141.645 million of 2025 net accounts-receivable growth less accounts-payable growth, equal to 51.5% of the $275.1 million anchor; durable portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A recurring incremental working-capital requirement must reduce owner earnings and therefore the anchor and every scenario's operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: The net decrease was primarily due to a $433 million increase in accounts receivable, a $77 million increase in prepaid expenses and other assets and a $64 million decrease in operating lease liabilities, partially offset by a $291 million increase in accounts payable.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a large 2025 cash requirement and similar receivables-versus-payables cash use in prior years, but the supplied valuation record does not demonstrate whether normalized working capital was deducted. Timing and tax-related balances mean the entire reported cash-flow change is not automatically recurring. The identified scale is nevertheless large enough to change the valuation materially if a meaningful portion is structural.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild 2016-2025 owner earnings with explicit changes in receivables, supplier payables and other operating balances; separate structural growth funding from timing, taxes, leases and supplier-financed capex, then refit the anchor and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Cash-only capex may omit supplier-financed asset additions
audit_findings.magnitude: $104.495 million of 2025 capitalized assets financed through accounts payable, equal to 34.2% of 2025 OE and 38.0% of the $275.1 million anchor; net omitted amount unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Unrecorded accrual-basis capital additions would reduce owner earnings, potentially lowering the latest-year ceiling, trend anchor and operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2025, we used $293 million of cash in investing activities, consisting of $197 million to purchase property and equipment, $79 million of net purchases of short-term investments, $13 million of investments in capitalized software and $4 million for the acquisition of certain assets accounted for as a business combination.
audit_findings.explanation: The supplier-financed additions are demonstrated by the filing, but their omission from owner earnings is not proven without the underlying worksheet and payable roll-forward. Their scale is material. Payments for prior-period financed additions must also be identified so the same investment is neither omitted nor deducted twice.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile annual property, equipment and software additions to cash purchases, supplier-financed additions and subsequent payable settlements for every OE year; deduct each addition exactly once, then recompute the OE series, anchor and scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The entire cash balance may not be excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.485333 billion added to the bridge, equal to $2.94 per diluted share and 27.8% of base equity value; required operating portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash needed for gross settlement timing, sequential-liability exposure and stress liquidity is an operating asset and should be excluded from the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: This collections and payments cycle may increasingly consume working capital if we continue to be successful in growing our business.
audit_findings.explanation: The operating model demonstrably creates substantial settlement exposure, including $3.201 billion of receivables versus $2.563 billion of payables at June 2026. However, the record does not establish a minimum operating-cash requirement, and the $745 million undrawn revolver may reduce that requirement. The potentially affected bridge amount is large, but materiality of the actual adjustment remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Prepare monthly and seasonal settlement-liquidity data, receivable aging, supplier payment terms, sequential-liability stress losses and revolver availability; determine minimum operating cash and rerun the bridge using only excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Existing uncertain-tax exposure is not visible in the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $115.566 million gross, of which $83 million reduces deferred-tax assets and approximately $33 million remains; $33 million equals about $0.07 per share and 0.6% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any legacy cash settlement not captured in forecast taxes would be deducted in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, our total amount of gross unrecognized tax benefits was $116 million before netting with deferred tax assets for tax credit carryforwards and is considered a long-term obligation.
audit_findings.explanation: The exposure is real, but omission of the full gross amount is not a demonstrated error because most offsets deferred-tax assets and settlement timing is uncertain. Even deducting the entire $115.566 million would reduce value by only about $0.23 per share, or 2.2% of base equity value, far below the $2.46 gap between the $11.97 bull value and the $14.43 market price.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the recorded net liability, settlement range and insurance or indemnification, and rerun only if expected cash payments plus penalties materially exceed the approximately $33 million net amount or are absent from forecast taxes.

audit_findings.title: Privacy litigation creates an unrecorded contingent claim
audit_findings.mechanism: Legacy damages and uninsured defense costs reduce the equity bridge, while recurring compliance costs or platform restrictions reduce OE and growth.
audit_findings.evidence: On December 18, 2025, the Court denied the Company’s motion to dismiss the consolidated amended complaint, except as to plaintiffs’ claim for declaratory relief, which the Court dismissed with prejudice.
audit_findings.explanation: Denial of most of the dismissal motion demonstrates that the litigation remains active, not that TTD is liable or that damages will be material. The latest filing places the case in discovery and supplies no damages range, insurance recovery or remediation cost. It may affect value, but the record cannot establish materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain counsel's loss range, class-size and damages analysis, insurance and indemnification limits, expected defense costs and potential operating remedies; bridge probable legacy costs and rerun OE and growth for recurring effects.

audit_findings.title: Stock-award tax benefits may distort the historical OE anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $73 million in 2024 versus $9 million in 2025, a $64 million swing equal to 23.3% of the $275.1 million anchor; normalizable portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Volatile exercise- and vesting-related tax benefits enter net income and historical OE, affecting the fitted trend anchor and all scenario values.
audit_findings.evidence: The extent of the impact may be subject to volatility resulting from changes in our stock price and volume of transactions by employees.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a large and volatile tax effect, but it does not establish that the entire benefit is nonrecurring because some tax deductions may accompany the continuing stock-compensation program. The 2024 benefit alone equals 22.2% of that year's $328.6 million OE, making the unresolved normalization reasonably capable of materially inflating the fitted anchor.
audit_findings.action: Separate ordinary deductions associated with recurring stock compensation from excess benefits or detriments for every OE year; normalize consistently with the forecast compensation and share-count policy, refit the anchor and rerun all scenarios.
